QMSBR—*Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral Research*—is a modular
collection of chapters designed to support more than one quantitative-methods
course. Its primary purpose is to help applied researchers read quantitative
studies; evaluating a study and learning how to conduct a clearer one are
secondary benefits. The chapters are maintained as one canonical set, so a
correction can improve every course route that uses it.

Part One covers foundations, regression, and generalized linear models.
Chapters 1--4 stay readable without running code; later chapters introduce
reproducible computing and regression where those tools serve a clear reading
or research purpose. Part Two covers factor analysis and latent-variable
modelling; Part Three is reserved for multilevel and longitudinal models. Study
design is addressed wherever it controls interpretation, but a named
statistical procedure never creates a causal claim. The reading approach the
chapters share is set out on
[The Argument-Based Approach](argument-approach.qmd).

## Citation {#citation}

> Chen, J. (2026). *QMSBR: Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral
> Research*. https://jinsong-chen.github.io/QMSBR/

Also cite the original datasets, software, and studies used by an analysis.

## Licences {#licences}

Chapter text, figures, and site prose are licensed under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Original R code is
licensed under the MIT License. Data generated by QMSBR simulations is
dedicated under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

Third-party items ship with this site and keep their own terms. The
student-outcome data in Chapter 1 is a curated subset of the dataset released
by Realinho and colleagues (UCI Machine Learning Repository, dataset 697) under
CC BY 4.0; the secondary-school example data in Chapter 2 is derived from the
UCI Student Performance dataset (Cortez, 2008) under CC BY 4.0; and `apa.csl`
comes from the CSL styles collection under CC BY-SA 3.0. The R-support pages
carry their own licence and data terms. Package datasets used in examples
are loaded from their R packages and are not redistributed here.

Full terms are in [LICENSE](https://github.com/Jinsong-Chen/QMSBR/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Accessibility

HTML is the preferred reading format: it provides responsive layout, headings,
search, link text, and selectable code. Downloadable PDFs are retained for
printing and annotation and are checked for reading order, document language,
bookmarks, metadata, and visual integrity. A navigation entry for a unit that
is not yet available is shown in a muted colour and marked as disabled, so it
is not announced or reached as a working link. Accessibility problems can be
reported through the repository issue tracker or by email.

## Using QMSBR in a course {#courses}

QMSBR is a source library, not a syllabus. Keep chapter identities stable and
let each course choose its own sequence and assessed work.

| QMSBR website | Your course space |
|---|---|
| Canonical current chapters | The term sequence and weekly instructions |
| Stable public links | Announcements and deadlines |
| Answer-free chapter exercises | Assessment, feedback, and answer keys |

Link to the website so students receive corrections automatically. Lecture
notes, solutions, and assessments stay in your own course space.
